sections.heading: PQ Transactions in Inclusion Lists
sections.summary: The 8 KB IL limit fits about one PQ transaction per IL, allowing up to 16 per slot without spec changes.
sections.body:
- PQ EL signatures are expected to be 5-7 KB each, meaning worst case only one PQ transaction fits per inclusion list under the current 8 KB size limit.
- With 16 IL committee members, up to 16 individual PQ transactions could be force-included per slot, which is considered adequate for early PQ adoption when few users will opt for PQ signatures.
- No FOCIL mechanism changes are required for this basic level of PQ transaction inclusion; it works with the existing design.
- Including PQ transactions at scale (many per IL) requires each IL to carry a STARK proof (~300 KB), which demands significant networking redesign.
  - This is only feasible after EIP-8288 aggregation and PQ CL proof infrastructure are both shipped.
  - The network would already need to handle large proofs on both EL and CL layers before FOCIL proof inclusion is practical.

sections.heading: Switching IL Signatures to Lean XMSS
sections.summary: Replacing BLS with lean XMSS adds 2.4 KB per IL and appears feasible with current P2P stack, but urgency is debated.
sections.body:
- Switching IL signatures from BLS to lean XMSS adds 2.4 KB to each inclusion list, which is manageable within the current propagation window (6-9 seconds into the slot).
- Thomas argued this is not urgent because a quantum attacker targeting FOCIL would need to crack keys of all 16 includers to equivocate for a single slot — low reward compared to attacking consensus or stealing funds.
- NC and Jun Song disagreed in chat, arguing postponing the switch just leaves unfinished work for later.
- Jihoon noted the switch should happen after lean XMSS is finalized and confirmed for CL use; the cryptographic schemes (both leanSPHINCS and lean XMSS) are still in flux.
- Thomas acknowledged that if lean XMSS is used elsewhere on the CL, adding it to FOCIL should not be a large incremental effort, but cautioned against letting it block the fork if the signature scheme is not yet ready.

sections.heading: EIP-8288 Phasing and Timeline
sections.summary: EIP-8288 is being split into three sub-EIPs: leanSPHINCS (possibly H-star), mempool aggregation via leanVM (I-star target), and leanPCS proofs (I-star or J-star).
sections.body:
- EIP-8288 is being rewritten into sub-EIPs because the original is too large to reason about as a single proposal.
- Part 1 — leanSPHINCS: individual PQ signatures for EL transactions, possibly shipping in H-star. Expected before aggregation is available.
- Part 2 — Mempool recursive aggregation (leanVM): target I-star, estimated mid-2028. leanVM formal verification and multiple implementations expected ready by July 2027.
- Part 3 — leanPCS (arbitrary proof aggregation): at best I-star, more likely J-star, as it is less urgent than signatures and aggregation.
- It is considered likely that PQ EL (leanSPHINCS without aggregation) ships before EIP-8288 aggregation, meaning individual large PQ signatures will exist in the mempool for a period.
- During this interim period, FOCIL can include a small number of unaggregated PQ transactions per IL without modification.

sections.heading: Bandwidth and IL Size Concerns Post-PQ
sections.summary: Including STARK proofs in ILs (~300 KB each, 16 per slot) would massively increase CL bandwidth; this is deferred until proof networking infrastructure exists.
sections.body:
- Mikhail raised concern that transitioning from raw PQ signatures to STARK proofs in ILs could suddenly increase each IL from ~7 KB to ~300 KB, straining CL bandwidth already under pressure from PQ consensus changes.
- Thomas clarified that FOCIL does not need to include proofs until after both EIP-8288 aggregation and PQ CL with aggregation are shipped; until then, raw individual transactions suffice.
- By the time proof inclusion in ILs is needed, the network should already be redesigned to handle large proof objects on both layers.
- Adjustable parameters to manage bandwidth: reducing IL committee size (trading off some censorship resistance), extending propagation windows, and bounding IL gas.
- Jihoon proposed a delayed inclusion constraint (n+1 slot instead of immediate next slot) to gain 12 extra seconds of propagation time, acknowledging this sacrifices a core EIP-7805 design value.
  - PQ Gasper already uses delayed aggregates inclusion with up to 18 seconds for propagation as precedent.

sections.heading: FOCIL Impact on Frames and Hegota Scoping
sections.summary: FOCIL in Hegota would delay frames somewhat, but Thomas argued the knock-on delay to the PQ fork is minimal, as PQ CL is far out.
sections.body:
- Thomas acknowledged FOCIL will add some delay to frames due to increased testing surface, but argued the delay would not significantly impact the PQ I-star fork timeline.
- The PQ CL component (whether PQ Gasper or PQDC) is expected to take considerable time regardless, reducing the marginal cost of shipping FOCIL alongside frames.
- Justin Florentine (Besu) noted that given how far along FOCIL already is, dropping it from Hegota would not meaningfully speed up PQ CL work.
- Marc (EL perspective) said the interaction between FOCIL and EIP-8288 aggregation will be the hardest part, but breaking 8288 into sub-EIPs simplifies things; he would support it.
- The ACDC call on Thursday (November 26) will discuss Hegota scoping, but a final decision is expected on December 10 to allow US-based developers (absent for Thanksgiving) to participate.

sections.heading: IL Equivocation Under PQ
sections.summary: Equivocation with 300 KB STARK-carrying ILs could flood the network; propagating only IL headers as equivocation evidence is a potential future optimization.
sections.body:
- If ILs carry STARK proofs and an includer equivocates, the network must handle double the already-large objects.
- Jihoon proposed propagating IL equivocation evidence as headers only, dropping transaction and proof bytes, saving approximately 308×2 KB per equivocation.
- This optimization is not considered necessary before the STARK proof era and adds protocol complexity (new gossipsub topic).
- Agreement that this belongs in the design space for future PQ FOCIL with proof inclusion, not for near-term shipping.

sections.heading: PQ Gasper vs. PQDC Decision
sections.summary: PQ Gasper is running on pq-devnet-0 but faces significant compromises; if still questionable in 2-3 months, the team may switch to PQDC.
sections.body:
- Etan noted in chat that the decision between PQ Gasper and PQDC has not been made; NC added that a PQDC spec does not even exist yet.
- pq-devnet-0 is currently running PQ Gasper; networking appears likely to be the main bottleneck but real numbers are still needed.
- Mikhail shared his personal view: PQ Gasper is feasible but likely requires uncomfortable compromises — longer slots, higher bandwidth requirements, or more advanced pubsub protocols.
  - If PQ Gasper still looks questionable in 2-3 months (by January), the team should consider switching to PQDC.
  - Advanced pubsub protocols would benefit PQDC as well but may be a hard requirement for PQ Gasper.
- Mehdi Aouadi stated in chat that PQ Gasper is "not looking great" based on the last 3 PQ sessions and devnet-0, and that PQDC would be better but more expensive; PQ Gasper could serve as a catastrophic fallback.
- Thomas raised the question of how much PQ Gasper work transfers to PQDC; Jihoon noted that some (devnet benchmarks) transfers well, but PQ Gasper-specific hacks likely do not.
- Jihoon urged timeboxing PQ Gasper-specific non-transferable work to avoid spending months on a potential dead end.

sections.heading: Next Call Scheduling
sections.summary: Next FOCIL breakout scheduled for December 8 (two weeks), before the December 10 ACDC where the final Hegota scoping decision is expected.
sections.body:
- Jihoon proposed meeting in two weeks (December 8) rather than one week; Thomas (in chat) had no strong preference on timing but wanted one more call before Christmas.
- The December 8 breakout falls before the December 10 ACDC call where the final decision on FOCIL in Hegota is expected.
- ACDC calls may pause for a few weeks at year-end (as happened in 2025); FOCIL breakouts would likely pause in sync.
- Whether FOCIL breakouts continue after the ACDC decision depends on the outcome — if FOCIL is dropped from Hegota, breakouts may no longer be needed.
